title: The truck and the end of a run
summary: The truck in R.E.P.O. is more than the way in: the game gives it its own doors, its own end-of-run screen and a healer inside, and it tracks how much each player got back to the extraction point.
body: The truck has doors of its own. They open with their own curve and their own sound, which is why boarding at the end of a run is a staged moment rather than a fade to a menu.

The end screen has defined pages. The game separates the start of the run from three endings: not enough hauled, enough hauled, and every player back aboard, so the game knows which ending you earned before it shows you one.
There is a healer inside. The truck carries a healer with its own hatch, lights and beam, which is why coming home is also how the crew recovers.

Hauling is tracked per player. The game keeps a record of each player's progress toward the extraction point, including the closest ring reached, so what you carried out is attributed rather than pooled blindly.
Arriving is acknowledged too. The game shows a short introduction as the crew reaches the shop, so the run has an ending on screen and not only in the score.
What this entry does not tell you: how much a run has to be worth, how long the doors take, or what the healer restores. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The truck has doors of its own, with their own animation and sound.
The end-of-run screen has defined pages covering the start, not enough, enough, and everyone aboard.
The truck contains a healer with its own beam and particles.
Progress toward the extraction point is tracked for each player.
A short shop introduction is shown as the crew arrives.
